Punch the Target Dummy

Proposal approved · revision 1

Mechanics

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.

Assumptions: Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter. The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested. The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target. Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics. Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility. No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

Theme

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.

Assumptions: No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default. Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

Environment & layout

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.

Assumptions: A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic. The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles. Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

EXPERIENCE DIRECTION
A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.

Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.
